quests.contextSentence: The two suppliers both sent samples, and they were delivered on the same day.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'they' is plural, but the suppliers are people who sent things. What was delivered on the same day is the samples.
quests.nativeTip: The passive verb 'were delivered' points to what travels.

quests.contextSentence: Kabir and Anya both applied, but only he was invited to interview.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Both' covers Kabir and Anya, but 'he' picks out one. It is Kabir, the male applicant.

quests.contextSentence: Both of the printers ran out of toner, so neither of them worked until the caretaker replaced it.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Both of the printers' establishes the pair. 'Neither of them' picks up the same pair.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'them' points back to ➔ 'the two printers'

quests.contextSentence: The guard told us that all the passengers had to have their seat belts checked before take-off.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Their' is plural and belongs to those being checked. The passengers own the belts; the guard is not one.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'their' points back to ➔ 'all the passengers'

quests.contextSentence: Some of the tickets were sold online, and they cost less than those bought at the door.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'they' is the subject compared with 'those bought at the door'. The comparison implies the online tickets.
quests.nativeTip: 'Those bought at the door' is the comparison. What is cheaper?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'they' points back to ➔ 'the tickets sold online'

quests.contextSentence: Some of the milk had spilled, but it hadn't reached the floor.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is singular and refers to the substance that spilled. The floor is where it might have gone, not what did the spilling.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the spilled milk'

quests.contextSentence: The guard reminded us that every employee must show their card at the gate.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Their' is the singular 'they', matching 'every employee'. The guard is giving the reminder.

quests.contextSentence: Every dish on the menu comes with a side, and you can swap it for salad.
quests.ruleExplanation: Consider the form of 'it': it is singular and refers to the item that can be swapped. That is the side, not the whole dish or menu.
quests.nativeTip: What can be swapped for salad?

quests.contextSentence: Every student got a certificate, and each one was signed by the principal herself.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Herself' emphasises the person who signed. The principal is the singular, feminine noun who did it.

quests.contextSentence: Many of the residents signed the petition, and several have since asked the organisers to remove their names.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Their names' are the names of the people who signed. Several of the residents are the ones asking for removal, whereas the organisers only receive the request.
quests.nativeTip: Whose names appear on the petition and are now being withdrawn?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'their' points back to ➔ 'several of the residents'

quests.contextSentence: Many tourists visit the temple, but few of them stay long enough to see the gardens behind it.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'it' is singular and non-human, so it is not 'many tourists'. The gardens are behind the temple.
quests.nativeTip: 'It' is singular. What are the gardens behind?

quests.contextSentence: The nurse checked on the patients, and a few of them needed extra blankets.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'A few of them' picks a subset from a group. The group is the patients; the nurse is one person and blankets are needed by people.

quests.contextSentence: We compared two offers. Either would work, but neither of them includes travel.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither of them' refers back to the pair. The two offers are the things being compared.
quests.nativeTip: 'Neither of them' picks from a pair.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'them' points back to ➔ 'the two offers'

quests.contextSentence: Neither Ivan nor Paula answered, but the message I left for them was clear.
quests.ruleExplanation: With 'neither... nor', the plural pronoun 'them' still refers to both people. The message was left for both.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'them' points back to ➔ 'Ivan and Paula'

quests.contextSentence: There are two candidates, and either could win if their supporters turn out.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'their' refers to the candidates, since it is they who have supporters. The supporters are the ones who turn out.
quests.nativeTip: 'Either' can point to each candidate. Whose supporters?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'their' points back to ➔ 'the two candidates'

quests.contextSentence: The workshop had thirty participants, some of whom had travelled overnight.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Some of whom' takes a subset from a group of people. The group is the participants.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'whom' points back to ➔ 'the thirty participants'

quests.contextSentence: The library received two hundred donations, most of which were textbooks.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Most of which' refers to the group just mentioned, the donations. Textbooks are what most of them were.
quests.nativeTip: 'Most of which' picks a majority. Of what?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'which' points back to ➔ 'the two hundred donations'

quests.contextSentence: The union represents drivers, all of whom must renew their licences every five years.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'All of whom' points to the group of people mentioned before. The union is an organisation, so it would need 'which'.
quests.nativeTip: Which noun is a group of people?

quests.contextSentence: The board is divided, but it has agreed to publish its report.
quests.ruleExplanation: A collective noun that takes 'is' is matched with singular 'it'. The board acts as one body here.
quests.nativeTip: A collective noun that takes a singular verb goes with a singular pronoun.

quests.contextSentence: The team have all been given new laptops, and they are delighted.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'They' is plural and refers to the members of the team, who are the ones to be delighted.

quests.contextSentence: The jury has reached its verdict, but the judge asked it to reconsider.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is singular, and the jury is treated as one unit here. The judge is the one asking.
quests.nativeTip: Who reached the decision, and who was asked to reconsider?

quests.contextSentence: Every participant received a name tag and was asked to wear it all day.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'it' is singular and non-human, so it is not the participant. A name tag is the thing you wear.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the name tag'

quests.contextSentence: Most of the staff are in on Fridays, but some work from home when they have deadlines.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' contrasts the majority with the minority. 'They' refers to the subject of that clause, some.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'they' points back to ➔ 'some of the staff'

quests.contextSentence: None of the trainees passed the test, but the examiner said all of them could retake it next month.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'it' is singular and non-human. What is retaken is the test, not the people or the examiner.

quests.contextSentence: All of the guests had arrived except the Hendersons, who had sent word that they would be late.
quests.ruleExplanation: Notice that 'who' points to the Hendersons, and 'they' is the subject of the message. The other guests had already arrived.

quests.contextSentence: Several of the interns asked their mentors for feedback, and most of them received it within days.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Most of them' takes a subset of a group. The recipients of feedback are the interns.

quests.contextSentence: Several bidders submitted offers, and the seller accepted the highest, which was well above the estimate.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' comments on the phrase just before it, the highest offer. The seller did the accepting.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'which' points back to ➔ 'the highest offer'

quests.contextSentence: Neither of the two banks would lend us money unless we could offer collateral, which we did not have.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' refers to the thing just before it, collateral. The banks and the money are not what was missing.

quests.contextSentence: Many of the visitors asked the guide questions, and she answered all of them patiently.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'All of them' takes a whole set. She answers questions, not people, so 'them' is the questions.

quests.contextSentence: Each of the co-authors read the draft, and every one of them suggested changes that the editor merged herself.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Herself' emphasises the person who did the merging. The editor is the singular, female subject.
